transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a supply-chain finance facility on the table today -- $6,000,000 in supplier invoices from our approved purchasing division. The preliminary proposal assumes 90% financing of eligible invoices, with ordinary supplier recourse and no special funding or screening controls. Before I make a final decision on whether this facility may launch and on what terms, I'd like to conduct our standard round-robin review. I'd like to hear from credit risk, legal, and finance operations in turn. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: I'd like to start, since credit risk has a material finding. I received the completed obligor-concentration assessment this morning. The single-obligor limit leaves exactly $4,000,000 of the invoice pool eligible, and the approved advance rate for that exposure is exactly 85%. This assessment has not yet been uploaded to the credit file, so I want to make sure the committee has this information before we proceed. In light of this, the preliminary proposal's assumption of 90% financing across the full $6,000,000 pool is not supportable under our concentration limits.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a material legal finding to share. I just received the signed anchor-buyer undertaking in a legal memo, and it contains two critical requirements: first, the program must be non-recourse to suppliers, and second, the buyer's payment direction must be acknowledged before the first funding. I have not yet circulated this memo to the committee, but given that the preliminary proposal assumes ordinary supplier recourse, this is a direct conflict that needs to be resolved before we can proceed. The facility terms will need to be revised to reflect non-recourse to suppliers, and the buyer's payment direction acknowledgment must be completed as a pre-funding condition.

transcript.text: I have a material finance operations finding to share. My operations team completed a workflow test this week, and it confirmed two operational constraints: first, funding can be released only twice weekly, and second, every invoice requires a 3-business-day hold for duplicate-invoice screening before funds can be disbursed. This test result has not yet been recorded in the launch checklist, so I want to make sure the committee has this information before we proceed. These constraints directly conflict with the preliminary proposal's assumption of no special funding or screening controls.
